# `solar.date()` {#fn-solar-date}

The JPL comparison in A05 matched all tested civil-day passages, including paired dates near a solstice. [A05 results](a05-solar-limits.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-solar-date)

```{=html}
<p>The Sun can pass the same declination on either side of a solstice. The search
covers the selected civil year from midnight UT, including its first instant and
excluding the start of the next year. Daily geocentric apparent solar declinations
bracket the annual turning points. The function refines each extremum against the
ephemeris and solves separately on either side, then reports the civil day of each
crossing. A tangency gives one date. Two crossings can share a calendar day.
The calculation uses no terrain or solar limb model.
</p>
<p>Astronomical positions require Swiss Ephemeris files covering the epoch. We
recommend installing <span class="pkg">swephRdata</span>; see <code>skyscapeR-package</code> for setup.
</p>
```

[Event definition and clock convention](fn-riseset.qmd).


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>dec</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>One or more declinations in degrees.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>year</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Year for which to do calculations. Historical labels such as <code>"3700 BC"</code> are accepted by <code>astroYear</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>calendar</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Calendar for sampling and output. G for Gregorian or J for Julian. Defaults to the package calendar, initially Gregorian.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Logical. Display progress or informational messages. Default <code>TRUE</code>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A character matrix with one column per reachable input, in input order. The rows
are Dec, Date1 and Date2, with Date3 added if three passages fall in one civil
year. Dates are chronological day/month labels. Unused date cells are missing.
The function stops if all requested declinations are unreachable.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/mechanics.R`.
